actions.intent: Keep provider initialization at the application boundary while preserving construction of the request consumer across all known callers.
actions.module_role: consumer factory interface and its call sites
actions.pre_state: The consumer factory requires provider configuration arguments, and production and tests pass those arguments at every construction site.
actions.post_state: The consumer factory accepts only its functional construction inputs, and known production and test callers use the reduced interface.
actions.validation: Diff all known Coder.create call sites and existing constructor-oriented tests to confirm removal of the obsolete argument; the suite could not be executed locally because dependencies were missing.
actions.description: Remove provider credentials from the consumer factory contract and migrate production and test callers to the configuration-independent constructor.

actions.intent: Apply a compatibility policy only to requests targeting the endpoint whose wire contract requires it, without misrouting other hosts that serve the same model family.
actions.pre_state: The affected endpoint falls through to a generic compatible-provider implementation, while model identifiers are insufficient to identify the actual endpoint.
actions.post_state: Exact canonical hostname and legitimate subdomains select the specialized adapter; unrelated, hostile-suffix, missing, and invalid URLs do not.
actions.validation: Route exact-host, subdomain, and hostile lookalike URLs through provider selection and assert their resulting request behavior distinguishes matched from fallback endpoints.
actions.description: Select an endpoint-specific compatibility adapter using parsed hostname boundaries rather than model-family names or substring matching.

actions.intent: Prevent regressions where normalization works in isolation but adapter output still hides or duplicates the provider reason.
actions.pre_state: The shared contract and adapter integrations have been implemented, but their behavior across error shapes and adapter tiers is not yet established.
actions.post_state: Tests specify that output preserves error stop state, includes HTTP status and body reason, excludes known opaque-only output, bounds long bodies, and avoids duplicate supplemental text.
actions.validation: The three added test files provide utility-level and representative adapter-level assertions; the available evidence does not include an executed test or CI result.
actions.description: Exercise utility edge cases and representative real adapter catch paths with opaque SDK messages that retain the actual reason in separate body fields.

actions.intent: Demonstrate that replaying a prior thinking turn no longer produces a rejected continuation request.
actions.pre_state: A multi-turn request includes an assistant thought that conversion represents as reasoning_content, and a strict endpoint rejects any assistant reasoning property.
actions.post_state: The continuation receives a successful response, with reasoning_content present and reasoning absent in the captured HTTP request.
actions.validation: Use a strict local HTTP server that returns the reported 400 validation payload if reasoning is present, then execute two turns through OpenAIContentGenerator and inspect the second request body.
actions.description: Exercise the complete history-conversion, provider-adaptation, and HTTP path against a strict contract oracle.

actions.intent: Allow one client integration to target provider-compatible endpoints that require additional SDK configuration without embedding startup configuration inside the request consumer.
actions.module_role: application configuration boundary and provider client initializer
actions.pre_state: The application boundary supplies only a key and base, while a downstream consumer factory owns provider SDK mutation and cannot represent type, version, deployment, or engine settings.
actions.post_state: Startup owns provider SDK initialization, exposes the supported endpoint settings, and mutates optional SDK attributes only when corresponding values were supplied.
actions.validation: Inspect parsed option definitions and the pre-construction mapping to provider SDK attributes; verify the downstream factory no longer accepts or assigns provider configuration. Runtime validation remains unavailable in the inspected environment.
actions.description: Accept endpoint-specific provider settings at the application boundary and apply only supplied values to the shared provider client before constructing downstream consumers.

actions.intent: Make provider-facing text, response, streaming, and image entry points consistently return actionable HTTP failure details.
actions.pre_state: Adapter catch blocks independently format thrown SDK values, and some lose bodies or duplicate supplemental details.
actions.post_state: Affected adapters consume the shared normalized diagnostic while preserving their established stop reasons, contextual prefixes, exception categories, hints, and nonduplicated supplemental data.
actions.validation: Mocked end-to-end catch-path tests require status and body propagation for representative image, text, response, and Bedrock tiers and require supplemental raw metadata to appear once.
actions.description: Replace adapter-local message-only formatting with the shared diagnostic contract while retaining adapter-specific semantics such as category prefixes, hints, and supplemental metadata.

actions.intent: Recover actionable HTTP failure details that provider SDKs retain outside Error.message.
actions.pre_state: A provider call has thrown an unknown value whose status and body may occupy SDK-specific fields or whose message may already contain the body.
actions.post_state: The failure is represented by a stable record with a safe message, optional numeric status, optional non-empty bounded body, and an explicit body-in-message predicate.
actions.validation: Synthetic error shapes verify field precedence and extraction for multiple SDK conventions, non-Error serialization, empty-body handling, truncation, and existing-body detection.
actions.description: Convert heterogeneous thrown provider values into one bounded diagnostic record containing the original message, optional HTTP status, optional body, and a flag indicating whether the message already carries that body.

actions.intent: Prevent strict-schema request rejection without discarding supported replay data, explicit caller intent, or shared history.
actions.pre_state: An inherited generic transformation has added a reasoning field equal to reasoning_content on an assistant history message, but the selected endpoint rejects reasoning and accepts reasoning_content.
actions.post_state: The outbound copy omits reasoning only when it exactly matches the derived mirror signature; reasoning_content and distinct explicit reasoning values remain, and the source request is unchanged.
actions.validation: Assert the mirrored-equality case is removed, unequal explicit values are retained, supported content remains present, source history is not mutated, and fallback providers preserve their prior behavior.
actions.description: At the outbound boundary, remove only a field recognizable as a derived mirror while retaining the endpoint-supported source field and distinct explicit values.

actions.intent: Expose the provider's actual HTTP reason without duplicating it or discarding established adapter context.
actions.pre_state: A normalized failure may contain status and body separately, may already include the body in its message, and may require an adapter-specific prefix.
actions.post_state: The diagnostic contains status plus body when separately available; otherwise it preserves the message, with the requested prefix and status where applicable, and does not print the body twice.
actions.validation: Formatter unit tests assert unprefixed and prefixed status/body output, preservation of messages already containing a body, and fallback behavior for non-Error values.
actions.description: Render a normalized failure so status and body are exposed when available while preserving prefixes, fallbacks, and messages that already contain the body.

actions.intent: Route requests through endpoints whose invocation contract requires a deployment identifier or engine identifier.
actions.pre_state: Provider requests include generic chat fields but omit endpoint-specific deployment and engine routing fields.
actions.post_state: Each configured routing identifier is included under the provider call's expected request keyword, while absent identifiers add no keyword.
actions.validation: Inspect the kwargs assembled immediately before request hashing and ChatCompletion.create; a dedicated behavioral test proving present and absent branches is not in the pinned change.
actions.description: Conditionally translate configured deployment and engine identifiers into per-request arguments at the provider invocation boundary.

actions.intent: Keep separate resume surfaces from interpreting the same persisted provider interface differently.
actions.pre_state: One resume surface manually reads only legacy top-level fields and billing identity, while another uses the canonical reader that understands the latest nested runtime route.
actions.post_state: The resume surface obtains provider, endpoint, and wire mode from the canonical resolver, while its existing model restoration, foreign-endpoint rejection, provider healing, reasoning, and service-tier behavior remains downstream.
actions.validation: The focused regression tests assert that Desktop/TUI and CLI select the same nested route for a stale-billing row, and that Desktop/TUI gives the nested route precedence over stale top-level keys.
actions.description: Replace a consumer-specific reconstruction of persisted provider metadata with the canonical session-route resolver before applying existing endpoint-safety and provider-healing logic.

actions.intent: Restore a resumed session on the provider interface most recently used by that session without discarding compatible legacy route metadata.
actions.pre_state: Session metadata may contain a newer nested runtime route, older top-level provider/endpoint fields, and a first-call billing identity that disagree or are only partially populated.
actions.post_state: A provider-bearing nested runtime route wins; otherwise top-level route fields are retained and a routable billing identity fills only a missing provider, while unroutable bare billing buckets do not become route identities.
actions.validation: Conflicting nested-versus-billing and nested-versus-top-level fixtures must resolve to the nested provider and wire mode, while the existing legacy switched-provider fixture must still discard an endpoint belonging to the previous provider.
actions.description: Normalize multiple persisted route representations into one provider/endpoint/wire tuple using explicit freshness precedence: the latest nested runtime route first, then legacy top-level fields, with a routable billing identity only filling a missing provider.

workflows.name: adapt-session-resume-to-a-versioned-provider-route
workflows.description: Establish one precedence-aware interpretation of persisted provider-interface state, then make each resume consumer delegate route extraction to it and validate conflicts between new and legacy representations.
workflows.goal: Resume a session using its latest persisted provider, endpoint, and wire protocol without regressing compatible legacy rows or existing endpoint-safety rules.
workflows.entry_state: A producer persists the latest route in a nested runtime object, but at least one consumer independently reconstructs the route from older top-level fields and a potentially stale billing identity.
workflows.exit_state: Persisted route precedence is centralized and all relevant resume consumers use it; conflicting-representation tests select the latest nested route and legacy endpoint-safety coverage remains intact.

workflows.description: Extend a provider-compatible client by centralizing endpoint configuration, reconciling consumer construction, and translating optional routing values only at the invocation boundary.
workflows.goal: Permit the same application to invoke a compatible provider endpoint whose SDK and request contracts require optional endpoint metadata, without forcing provider configuration through the consumer factory.
workflows.entry_state: The client supports a generic key/base configuration, configuration mutation occurs inside a downstream factory, and provider-specific routing values cannot reach the request call.
workflows.exit_state: Application startup initializes all supplied provider settings, the consumer factory is configuration-independent, known callers use its revised interface, and configured request-routing identifiers are forwarded conditionally.

workflows.name: adapt-generic-compatible-requests-to-a-stricter-endpoint-contract
workflows.description: Introduce a narrowly routed outbound adapter when a nominally compatible endpoint rejects a generic provider transformation, preserving shared semantics and verifying the complete continuation path.
workflows.goal: Allow thinking-history and tool-call continuations to satisfy the stricter endpoint schema without weakening behavior for other compatible endpoints or deleting supported replay data.
workflows.entry_state: A generic compatible-provider transformation derives an extra message field from preserved history, and the actual endpoint rejects that field during multi-turn continuation.
workflows.exit_state: The affected endpoint is safely identified, only the derived incompatible field is removed from an outbound copy, other endpoint behavior is unchanged, and a strict HTTP oracle accepts the continuation wire shape.

workflows.name: surface-hidden-http-error-details-at-provider-boundaries
workflows.description: Establish one bounded error contract, compose it without duplication, adopt it at affected provider boundaries while preserving local behavior, and verify both utility semantics and representative catch paths.
workflows.goal: Return actionable provider HTTP failure details when an SDK exposes the status and response body outside its opaque Error.message.
workflows.entry_state: Multiple provider adapters own incompatible catch formatting, and gateway or proxy failures can expose only an opaque SDK message even though the thrown object retains a status and body.
workflows.exit_state: Affected adapters expose a bounded status/body diagnostic without double-printing existing content and without losing adapter-specific prefixes, categories, hints, stop reasons, or supplemental metadata.
